utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, you spent five days in Cecelija; is that right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the course of those five days, was there any fighting going on between the KLA and our forces? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: There were no clashes during those five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No clashes. Why, then, did the KLA withdraw from the village and decided to withdraw its forces from the area, from the region?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: You're asking me? During the five days when we were there, there were no clashes, but after those five days, then the fighting began, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Between whom?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: This question is so awkward. I don't know exactly what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that the fighting began. Between whom? The fighting between whom?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: As far as I know, I didn't say that combat began; I said there were no confrontations for five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you said: "And five days later, the fighting began." "After those five days, then the fighting began." That's what you said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I didn't say that combat began, but that after five days we heard that -- we heard that there had been fighting throughout the area. So please do not hurry me. Now ask whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you. So throughout that time, you were -- you spent your time together with the KLA; right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Spent most of the time with civilians, with unarmed civilians. The KLA was positioned lower down. It wasn't so close to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But I'm asking you now. Let me ask you in a different way. When they decided to withdraw, that is to say, when the KLA decided to withdraw, you decided to leave the region and go from Gornja Studime [phoen] in the direction of Donja Studime [phoen]; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: You are complicating this. Donja e Eperm [phoen]? I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You went to another village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let him mention the names of the villages clearly. I don't understand which village he means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, your time now is coming up, but you can ask two more questions if you want.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have many more questions, but as you can hear, the witness doesn't seem to understand a single question. He is receiving interpretation in the Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want to ask another two questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have 32 more questions, or more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The Bench will give you ten minutes more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, what direction did the KLA leave in?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: The KLA withdrew into the hills, for tactical reasons, in order to save the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did they leave the population or did they carry on with the population?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: No. The KLA, in order to prevent worse from happening, left the population after the population had decided to go downhill, down to the village of Studime and to continue in the direction of Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that two kilometres after a certain place on the way to Vucitrn, that you came across some Serb policemen. Do you remember having said that, that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: If possible, could I have the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the way towards Vucitrn, you came across some Serb policemen. That's what you say in your statement. Moving along in that group that was heading towards Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Serbian forces came down from Shala and shelled us, and we fled to Studime e Eperme. We rested for a moment and formed a convoy and decided to go in the direction of Vushtrri. At Studime --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am skipping over the questions because my time has been restricted. Now, I'm asking you about the event when you came across some policemen, and you say that they did not stop you but they just directed you towards your road to Vucitrn. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: This question is very mixed up and unclear. Slowly, please. One by one, I will explain these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't argue. Mr. Milosevic, it will help us: Which part of the statement are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the statement in front of me, but there is a portion of his statement where he says, "We came across Serb policemen." They did not stop them but directed them towards Vucitrn and the factory farm there, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That's clear enough. Did a group of Serb policemen direct you towards the factory farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just before going out onto the main Mitrovica-Prishtina road, these policemen pointed us towards the agricultural cooperative, where they gathered us and left us in the open air all night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You claim that that agricultural cooperative was guarded by civilian policemen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Can I have the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that the agricultural cooperative was guarded by the civilian police force.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that in my statement. I said that the police were inside and the army joined them, so there were police and military together, and civilians too. I didn't say that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what were the civilians doing?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Which civilians do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Those civilians that you just mentioned, that you said there were police and military together, and civilians too. Those civilians.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: They only moved back and forth, and at that moment, they weren't doing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend exactly in the prison in Smrekovnice?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Excuse me. Yes, clear. I was in the Smrekovnice Prison from the 3rd of May to the 23rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you spent 20 days there. Now, is it true that one of the guards was an Albanian by the name of Agron?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes. There was a prison warden called Agron.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was he an Albanian?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I didn't know him. I only knew him as Agron.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, was he an Albanian? Even if you didn't know him, you met him.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: According to his name, he should be an Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So an Albanian was guarding you while you were in prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said that the guard was called Agron.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You claim that in the prison in Smrekovnice, you answered the investigator that you had no knowledge about the KLA and its members. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The accused is asking such long questions that I can't distinguish one sentence from another. Please give me one plain sentence to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did you tell the interrogator in the prison that you had no knowledge about the KLA and its members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said in prison that I wasn't a member of the KLA but I had helped them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You told him that you had given them money. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I said that I had helped them, and it is indeed true that, within my own resources, I helped them of my own free will, because the KLA was -- it was the KLA that fought for the freedom of Kosova, with the help of NATO and the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That means that they didn't ask you for money; you gave them money of your own free will.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Of my own free will, I wanted to help the army of the people. This was an army that defended people's homes, defended the people. It came from out of the people themselves. So I helped them out of my own free will, without any kind of coercion. It was my own free will. I say it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've had your ten minutes. Mr. Tapuskovic, have you any questions of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do have some questions because Mr. Slobodan Milosevic did not touch upon the second statement at all, and I do not wish to abuse the time, of course, but could you just tell me how much time I have at my disposal, because this is a very important statement for the issues you're going to deal with. Some very important things have been left out which are contained in that second statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's get on with it now and finish it this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll do my best, but I have to go back for a moment, actually, to the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gani -- I'm going to refer to you by your first name. It's easier. I hope you don't mind if I refer to you by your first name. But could we first clarify this fact, that is to say, when did you stop working at your work post where you were employed? In your first statement, dated the 28th and 29th of May, 1999, in the first sentence of that statement, you said that you worked as a technician until the 24th of March, 1999: "I was employed at the hydroelectric power station as section manager." Today you said something else, something different. Now, could you tell me, which is correct: What you said today or what you said then?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: We worked until 12 April. As of 24th of March -- allow me to give you an explanation. With the beginning of the NATO bombing on the 24th of March, our timetable changed. I went to go to work every three or four days. That's why I said I stayed in my workplace until the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Further on, in paragraph 3, you said that on the 24th of March, you heard on television that NATO had started to bomb. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then, during the following days, you heard several explosions coming from the direction of Pristina, and you say, "... which I presumed were NATO attacks." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I can explain that. On the 24th of March, I heard the NATO bombs, but I still went to work. This is the reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that of any significance, that you decided, together with your family, to leave the place where these bombs were falling, or was this not significant?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just a moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness described how he heard bombs falling from the direction of Pristina. At no time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The witness described how he heard the sound of bombs falling from the direction of the city of Pristina. At no time -- and we are referring here to NATO bombs, the NATO bombardment. I think it needs to be clarified whether Mr. Tapuskovic is referring in his last question to NATO bombs or bombs or shells fired by the Serb forces. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put the question again so we can understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need for me to rephrase it, Your Honours, because it says here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have asked you to rephrase it, so kindly do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I will, Your Honour, but this is verbatim what his statement says: "During the days that followed --" this is what he said. I have no reason to interpret it: "During the days that followed, I heard several explosions coming from the direction of Pristina, 15 kilometres away, which I presumed were NATO attacks." That is literally what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now, was this of significance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is whether -- the fact that he presumed that he heard NATO bombing, whether that affected his decision to leave together with his family so that he would seek shelter from the place where these bombs were falling. That's my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to be brief. Every Albanian I think was looking forward to NATO bombing, because he hoped and they hoped that it would bring their freedom. I don't know where the mistake is, but the fact is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no mistake. It's been suggested because you heard the explosions, you were fleeing from the explosions. If the answer is no, just say no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it may appear so, but I did not leave because of NATO bombing but because of the shelling by the Serb forces. We could tell between the NATO bombing and the shelling. These are two different things. I want to make it clear that we did not go away because of NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gani, please, I'm just asking you to give me answers that are as brief as possible, bearing in mind the time involved. Now we have this other statement of yours given on the 10th of October, 2001. On page 2 of that statement, the English version also page 2, paragraph 2, you said here: "Altogether I think that in the village of Cecelia, there were about 2.000 people who had sought shelter there." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, am I allowed to look at the statement? Because I am not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is obviously going to go on. Would you have a copy of the statement for the witness so he can look at it? Would you get the passage out. We'll adjourn for ten minutes, we'll have a break for the interpreters, and then we'll go on until you finish, Mr. Tapuskovic. Yes, ten minutes. --- Break taken at 4.08 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Has the witness got the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe he does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What language has he got it in?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He's got it in Albanian, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have you found the passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We have, Your Honour, and it's been highlighted in yellow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And in the English, where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the English, it is on page 2 of the statement that is dated 10 October 2001. Close to the bottom of the page, beginning with the words, "Altogether..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, Mr. Tapuskovic, we can go on until 5.00, so would you kindly bring your cross-examination to an end by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I shall certainly finish much earlier, and I shall certainly be putting very direct questions, so I'm sure to finish before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Gani, I asked you a while ago, because that's what it says in your statement. It says here, page 2, paragraph 2 - I don't know where it is in your version - but in Cecelia, there were about 7.000 people. Is that right, civilians? That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes. Approximate number of civilians who stayed in Cecelia for about five days. This is what this figure is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when you came to Gornja Studime [phoen] right from Cecelija, together with the people who were there, as you had put it in your first statement, not to go back to that, there were a total of 10.000 to 15.000 people there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, but I want to give an explanation here too, because other people joined the column of people, so the number grew constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I understand. These are mainly people who came, as you put it in the first statement, they came from various places. I don't have to go into all of that. Drenica, et cetera, et cetera. Just look at page 1 and you'll see all the places that you mentioned. They came from different places.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Here it says about 7.000 people who were refugees in Ceceli. But when the column of people started to move downwards, then other people joined it, people who were spread in other villages, in Studime e Eperme, the mountains. So spontaneously the number of the people in the column grew, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's not dwell on that too long. Again on this same page, in paragraph 3 - so we're skipping one paragraph - you said when you were in Cecelia, that the KLA told you that you would stay there only temporarily. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you were waiting. You were waiting for them to tell you when you're supposed to leave; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: We weren't waiting for someone to order us; we were waiting, thinking that we were sheltered and protected there. At the first moment that we felt unsafe, then the KLA withdrew and we left for Studime.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then further on you said - this is paragraph 6 - that you stayed in that village for five days, in Cecelija. "When the KLA told us that the front line was broken at Shala and that the Serb forces had broken through." Is that when you had to leave, due to those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: It is explicitly stated in my statement that after the news was confirmed that the front line was broken at Shala, then we felt unsafe and then left for -- left Studime to go to a town or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Already in the following paragraph it says, literally: "At that time --" while you were in Cecelija, that is. "At that time, I did not see any evidence of civilian deaths in Cecelija." Is that right, that at that time in Cecelija there were no civilian casualties during those five days?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: As far as I know, there weren't any casualties, with the exception of one victim. I don't know how he was killed. That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You've explained that. I'll get to that a bit later. But now, after two paragraphs, you say: "While I was in Cecelija, I saw KLA fighters. I don't know how many there were, but some wore KLA uniform, others wore civilian clothing." I'm interested in the ratio. How many were in civilian clothing and how many were in uniform? And they all belonged to the KLA. Who outnumbered who?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: The KLA staff had more members dressed in uniform. There were few civilians, who were waiting maybe to get weapons or I don't know what. They were exercising.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, you're talking about weapons and you say which weapons the members of the KLA had. Is this true, what it says here, that there were M-48 rifles and then Kalashnikovs. "And I also saw one hand-held grenade launcher. It is the type that is fired from the shoulder. They also had hand grenades." Did the majority of KLA members have these weapons?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm interested in one more thing here. On page 4, on page 4 -- the English version is the 14th paragraph of page 3. It says here: "In Cecelija, I heard that in the village -- I heard that the dead body of a KLA fighter had been brought into the village. I was told that he was killed in Sllakofc or Shala area." Did you see that or did you only hear about that?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I only heard that the dead body was brought and was buried in Ceceli.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I am compelled to go back to the first statement, just one single paragraph in the first statement. That is page 3, the second paragraph in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Over here, you stated, and I have to read this out to you so that I could ask you something. You said that you stayed in Cecelija for five days, and "during which time the KLA suffered such heavy losses to the Serb forces that they told us that we had better leave the area." That's what you stated. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: In my statement I have said that we heard the news that in Shala there were losses inflicted on the KLA, and because of that, we were not safe to stay in Ceceli and then decided to leave to safer places.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have to highlight this. You said here that during these five days in Cecelija, "the KLA suffered such heavy losses to the Serb forces," et cetera. So can you tell us how many people lost their lives, how many KLA members lost their lives?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I don't know about this loss. I just heard it from rumours, because Shala is very far away from Ceceli.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You've heard just now that there were heavy losses among the KLA.

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: This is what we heard. These were the rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So there were considerable casualties, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's what he said he heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just interested in one more thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In this second statement, you described everything the way you had put it in the first statement. However, in this second statement, you did not mention at all that you had seen machine-gun fire aimed at civilians. You did not mention that in your second statement at all. How do you explain that? You said everything else, but you just did not say when the convoy stopped with that white flag, you were standing there for two hours, and in the second statement you did not mention at all that there was any shooting at civilians, but you did say it in the first statement. So how do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I object?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It clearly says, at the very beginning of the second statement given by this witness that: "This statement is being made to clarify some matters that have come up in the prior statement." At the top of the page, a sentence that stands by itself. Now, given that context, I believe this question is a bit unfair to the witness. He had no reason to mention every detail in the second statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That answers the question, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but he repeated everything else, everything except for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I do have to ask you, Mr. Gani: Did you see any shooting against people? Did you see people who were being shot at, unarmed people?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: At what point in time are you asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when you were on the road in that column of people, when you stopped, and when the white flag was raised. In this other statement, you said that you stood there at that point for two hours, and then you continued your journey. In this second statement, you only said that you stood there for two hours, but you did not mention any shooting whatsoever in your second statement. So is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: We stayed there two hours. Then, after two hours, we decided to raise the white flag, as I say, because we were unprotected. And so we decided to go to the main road from Prishtina to Mitrovica, and then to leave Kosova. During those two hours, I didn't hear any shooting, but we felt defenceless and we had not eaten anything. We had no food, nothing to drink, so we had to find a solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you continued towards Smrekovnice, was there any shooting, up to the prison?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, we are still at Studime e Eperme, before the massacre was committed. Although we had the white flag, despite that, the massacre was still perpetrated. What you are talking about happened after that night when we spent at the agricultural cooperative, when we males were taken to the prison, while we knew nothing about the children and the women. So there is a difference from the events in that place to that in the agricultural cooperative, and then we surrendered before we entered the agriculture cooperative. But it is regarded the while flag, and what happened, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you one more thing and that will be the end. On the road, did you see any shooting? That's what I'm asking you. Were you stopped by the white flag? Did you see any people being shot at there?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: When we had the white flag, after two hours that we started to move downwards, and when we entered Studime, they took away the flag and then they began to maltreat us, to kill, to injure people, and so on. We showed the white flag before we surrendered, but nevertheless, they did what they wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you saw 50 people who had lost their lives?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: Yes, about 50 people. I saw them, sir, after they broke loose the column of people, after they took away the white flag, then they started to maltreat us. So after the flag was taken away, the people continued to walk in the column, and then they were subjected to this massacre, looting, raiding, and everything I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will be brief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj, you just mentioned -- rather, you just described how "they" took away the white flag and began to maltreat us, to kill and so on. Just so that the record is clear, because pronouns are difficult, who is "they"? What do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: It's very clear. The Serb army of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And earlier on, you mentioned that you -- when you were in the village of Cecelija, you heard rumours or news that in a place called Shala, that losses had been inflicted on the KLA, so that it was no longer considered safe to stay in the village of Cecelija. If you know, and only if you know: Approximately how far is this place called Shala from Cecelija?

utterances.speaker: Gani Haradinaj
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact figure, but I think it's over ten kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj, thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. It's now concluded and you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you, this Trial Chamber. Thank you for enabling me to come here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Half past 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of May, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.43 p.m.,
